title: Masterwork gates: Forge +13..+15 and the SS->SSS rank-up need a home master
description:
WHY
Owner rulings, 2026-09-23:
- "only the ones with calling can make masterwork(the final tier)"
- The Forge's +13 to +15 band needs a master smith who is home.
- SS->SSS needs a master priest (calling rites, skill 5) who is stationed at the Sanctum and home. The owner chose this knowingly, against the designer's and the director's advice.
Both gates change today's game. A level-5 Forge stops at +12 without a master, and the SSS goal gains a prerequisite. So they get their own bead and their own review.
Design: GAME_SPEC.md § Heroes staff the buildings (the masterwork table, and "The Rites gate touches the spine"). Numbers: SYSTEMS.md § Keepers and professions (Masterwork, and The Rites gate against the spine). Boundaries: DECISIONS.md 2026-09-23 (town), item 5, "Masterwork is a gate checked in the mutator".

BEHAVIOR
1. New balance row: forge_masterwork_floor (12).
2. Forge gate:
   - Item.compute_enhance_cap takes a master flag: min(3 * forge_level, 15 if master else 12).
   - enhance_item and bulk enhance pass GameSession.keeper_is_master(&"Forge") (from ig-wgj.10).
   - Item.clamped_enhance_level stays at 15, so gear already at +13 to +15 keeps its level.
   - The Forge panel says why the cap stops at +12: "Masterwork (+13 to +15) needs a born smith at skill 5 working here."
3. Rites gate:
   - rank_up_hero (game_session.gd:387) refuses SS->SSS unless keeper_is_master(&"Sanctum").
   - Every other rank-up is unchanged.
   - Heroes already at SSS keep their rank. Nothing re-checks on load.
   - The target may be the priest itself.
   - The Sanctum panel's RankUp control says why it is refused: "SS->SSS needs a born master priest working here."
4. Both checks sit inside the mutators. The UI only reflects them.

ACCEPTANCE
- Forge tests, all with a level-5 Forge:
  - enhancing +12 -> +13 is refused with no keeper, with a non-calling skill-5 smith, with a calling smith below 5, and with a calling master who is away
  - it is allowed with a calling master who is home
  - an item already at +14 keeps +14 after the master leaves, and after a real save and reload
  - bulk enhance obeys the same cap
- Rites tests, with an SS target and enough Essence:
  - SS->SSS is refused with no keeper, with a non-calling skill-5 priest, with a calling priest below 5, and with a calling master who is away (dispatched)
  - it is allowed with a calling master who is home, including when the target is the master
  - F->D through S->SS are unchanged with no keeper
  - a refused rank-up spends no Essence
  - an SSS hero in a save loads as SSS with no priest
- Existing tests:
  - The enhance tests in tests/unit/test_equipment.gd that take a level-5 Forge past +12 either get a master-smith fixture or stop at +12. Say which, per test.
  - No existing test ranks a hero to SSS through rank_up_hero (grep, 2026-09-23). If one appears before this lands, it gets a master-priest fixture.
- BUILT: the import gate shows zero errors and zero warnings, and GUT is green.
- A verifier pass is mandatory. It touches the rank-up path, which is the spine, and the enhance cap; boundary #1 covers the save/reload proofs.

title: Keeper bonuses and XP: a home keeper boosts its building and levels up
description:
WHY
A keeper has to matter. With this bead, a keeper who is home adds a skill bonus to its building and earns XP by working. It also adds the master check that the masterwork beads (.12 gates, .11 draughts) call.
Numbers: SYSTEMS.md § Keepers and professions. Boundaries: DECISIONS.md 2026-09-23 (town), item 5.
The masterwork gates moved to their own bead, ig-wgj.12, on 2026-09-23. They change today's game (Forge stops at +12, SSS needs a priest), and they deserve their own review.

BEHAVIOR
1. New balance rows:
   - keeper_skill_bonus_levels (0.5)
   - alchemy_cost_cut_per_skill (0.10)
2. GameSession gets:
   - keeper_skill(building_id) -> int: the skill of the building's keeper in that building's profession. It is 0 with no keeper, or while the keeper is busy.
   - keeper_is_master(building_id) -> bool: a keeper who is home and passes Hero.is_profession_master for that building's profession. Nothing gates on it yet.
3. Pass the keeper skill as one more argument into the formula that already reads each building's level:
   - Forge: Item.compute_salvage_yield. Callers: salvage_item (game_session.gd:269) and every preview.
   - Sanctum: Hero.compute_essence_yield. Callers: sacrifice_hero (:379) and every preview.
   - Training Hall: the XP multiplier (:1454).
   - Reliquary: the lifetime only, never the damage chance. Covers LostCache.seconds_remaining callers (:1194, :1643) and _incident_remaining_seconds (:925). The damage chance at :190 stays untouched.
   - Apothecary: the draught parts cost, max(1, roundi(base * (1 - 0.10 * skill))).
   Grep every caller of each formula first. A preview must pass the same skill as the settled action, or the preview and the result stop agreeing.
4. Hands off: summon weights, the Reliquary damage chance and the enhance cap (the cap is .12's job).
5. XP: in GameSession._advance_clocks_in_memory (the live tick), every keeper who is home calls Hero.add_profession_xp for its building's profession with delta_seconds. _advance_orders_in_memory (the catch-up after the game was closed) grants none.
6. Each building's panel shows:
   - the keeper's current bonus, for example "Mira: salvage +15%"
   - the XP left to the next level
   - a Master badge when keeper_is_master is true

ACCEPTANCE
- Tests:
  - each of the 5 formulas at skill 0, 3 and 5 matches the SYSTEMS tables, including the Alchemy table
  - a keeper who is away gives 0, and keeper_is_master is false for them
  - keeper_is_master is true only for a calling keeper at skill 5 who is home
  - with a skill-5 keeper, summon weights, the damage chance and the enhance cap are unchanged
  - each preview equals its settled result
  - XP accrues on the live tick at x4 in the calling and x1 otherwise, and an offline catch-up of any length grants 0
- It survives save and reload: XP and skill are the same after a real disk round-trip through SaveService (APPDATA redirected).
- BUILT: the import gate shows zero errors and zero warnings, and GUT is green.
- A verifier pass is mandatory: boundary #1, plus the rescue-window lifetime, which decides when a stranded hero dies (next to boundary #3).

title: Station a keeper from the building panel (protected, still sendable)
description:
WHY
The owner wants heroes to run the shops (GAME_SPEC.md § Heroes staff the buildings). This slice lets you put a hero behind a counter, and makes that hero protected but still sendable. Boundaries: DECISIONS.md 2026-09-23, item 5.

BEHAVIOR
1. New Hero field station: StringName. &"" means no station. It holds a town building id: the node names in hub/town/town.tscn (Forge, Sanctum, TrainingHall, Reliquary, Apothecary).
2. GameSession gets:
   - station_hero(hero, building_id) -> bool
     - Refuses a building that takes no keeper (SummoningCircle, TownGate, or an unknown id) and a hero not on the roster.
     - Replaces the current keeper: the old keeper's station clears.
     - Moves a hero who already keeps another building.
   - unstation_hero(hero)
   - keeper_for(building_id) -> Hero or null, by scanning the roster
   All three mutate through the same profile-commit path the other mutators use, and emit roster_changed.
3. is_hero_protected(): a station counts. Sacrifice and bulk sacrifice refuse a keeper, and the UI gives the reason "Keeps the <building>".
4. NOT in is_hero_busy(), and no change to the 4 dispatch paths: dispatch_expedition, dispatch_force/_preview_force_data, dispatch_rescue, recover_cache. A keeper can be sent out, and its station stays set while it is away.
5. Permadeath: nothing is added to kill_hero(). The station leaves with the hero. Prove it with a test, and do not add cleanup code.
6. On load:
   - if two heroes claim one building, the first in roster order keeps it and the others are cleared with push_warning
   - an unknown building id is cleared with push_warning
7. UI:
   - Each staffable building's panel (Forge, Sanctum, Training Hall, Reliquary, Apothecary) gets a Keeper row:
     - the keeper's name, calling and skill in this profession, or "Away" while the keeper is busy
     - "Assign keeper" opens the shared roster picker, showing each hero's skill here and marking callings
     - "Unassign"
   - The hero detail shows the hero's calling, all five skills and its station.
   - The dispatch preview lists every keeper in the selection: "Runs without its keeper while away: Forge (Mira)". This is not a modal.

SAVE
- Additive key "station" in Hero.to_dict/from_dict. Missing means none.
- Do not bump SAVE_VERSION.

ACCEPTANCE
- It survives save and reload: station a hero, save through SaveService to disk (APPDATA redirected), reload, and the same hero keeps the same building.
- A save without the key loads with no keepers.
- Tests:
  - one keeper per building
  - moving a hero moves its station
  - unstation
  - sacrifice refuses a keeper, single and bulk
  - a keeper can be dispatched through each of the 4 dispatch paths, and still keeps the station after it returns
  - after kill_hero() on a keeper, keeper_for() returns null and no station code outside kill_hero ran
  - a duplicate-claim load
  - an unknown-id load
- A screenshot of a building panel showing its Keeper row, in .agent-results/<id>/.
- BUILT: the import gate shows zero errors and zero warnings, and GUT is green.
- Boundaries #1 (save), #2 (panels) and #3 (the permadeath path must stay single-writer) make a verifier pass mandatory.

FILES

- tests/unit/test_hub_controls.gd

keeper bonuses and work (the next bead); keepers drawn in town; Circle or Gate keepers; more than one keeper per building.

title: Profession skills: calling, XP, masterwork check, and save round-trip
description:
WHY
Owner rulings, 2026-09-23:
- "I want the heroes themselves be the shopkeep NPCs, they have their own blacksmith skills, research skills, ect"
- "Born + practice. The calling is an immense xp boost, like the progression system in rim world. Also only the ones with calling can make masterwork(the final tier) equips/food/etc"
Design: GAME_SPEC.md § Heroes staff the buildings. Numbers: SYSTEMS.md § Keepers and professions. Boundaries: DECISIONS.md 2026-09-23, item 5.
The data comes first. Every staffing slice reads these fields, and they cross save boundary #1.

BEHAVIOR
1. Five profession ids, each mapped to the building id that ig-wgj.1 uses. Those ids are the node names in hub/town/town.tscn:
   - smithing -> &"Forge"
   - rites -> &"Sanctum"
   - drill -> &"TrainingHall"
   - tracking -> &"Reliquary"
   - alchemy -> &"Apothecary"
   Keep them in one const table on Hero, like STAT_NAMES.
2. New Hero fields:
   - calling: StringName
   - profession_xp: Dictionary[StringName, float], XP seconds per profession
3. Calling = the profession at index (instance_id.hash() mod 5), in profession-table order.
   - It is set at creation.
   - It is re-derived in from_dict when the save has no valid calling. from_dict overwrites instance_id, so derive after that.
   - No summon RNG draw is added.
4. Static helpers on Hero, following the SYSTEMS table:
   - profession_skill(hero, profession, balance) -> int: level k costs 20*k XP-minutes, capped at 5. The scale is the same for every hero and every profession.
   - add_profession_xp(hero, profession, work_seconds, balance): adds work_seconds * calling_xp_multiplier when profession == calling, otherwise work_seconds * 1.0. Nothing calls it yet; ig-wgj.10 wires it to the live tick.
   - is_profession_master(hero, profession, balance) -> bool: calling == profession and skill == 5.
5. New balance rows in balance_table.gd and balance.tres:
   - profession_xp_minutes_per_level (20.0)
   - profession_skill_cap (5)
   - calling_xp_multiplier (4.0)
6. Combat never reads these fields. compute_final_stats, hero_power and the forecast stay untouched.

SAVE
- Additive keys in Hero.to_dict/from_dict:
  - "calling": a String
  - "profession_xp": String -> float, with sorted keys so the output is stable
- A missing key gives the derived calling and no XP.
- An unknown profession id is dropped with push_warning.
- A negative or non-number XP value is reported with push_error and loads as 0. Match the existing validation style in from_dict.
- Do not bump SAVE_VERSION (P2-23 precedent).

ACCEPTANCE
- Tests:
  - The calling is stable for a given instance_id and is always one of the five.
  - Over 1000 new heroes, each profession gets 150-250.
  - profession_skill steps up at 20, 60, 120, 200 and 300 XP-minutes, and stays at 5 past that.
  - add_profession_xp with 60 s of work gives 240 XP-seconds in the calling and 60 in any other profession.
  - is_profession_master is true only for the calling at skill 5. A non-calling profession at skill 5 is not a master.
  - compute_final_stats is identical for two heroes that differ only in their profession fields.
  - The existing seeded summon tests pass unchanged.
- It survives save and reload:
  - to_dict -> from_dict keeps the calling and the XP.
  - A real disk round-trip through SaveService (APPDATA redirected) keeps them too.
  - An old save without the keys loads with derived callings and zero XP. After the next save and reload, the calling is the same one.
- BUILT: the import gate shows zero errors and zero warnings, and GUT is green.
- Boundary #1 makes a verifier pass mandatory.

FILES
- heroes/hero.gd
- balance_table.gd, balance.tres
- new: tests/unit/test_hero_professions.gd
- tests/unit/test_save_service.gd, only if the disk round-trip belongs there

NON-GOALS
stations; any UI; keeper bonuses; accruing XP on the tick; masterwork gates; a Circle keeper; research (parked for the base builder).
notes:
2026-09-23 OWNER RULINGS (director relay): Q1 keepers CAN go on expeditions; the shop runs without them, and death erases the skill (option A). Q2, owner's words: 'Born + practice. The calling is an immense xp boost, like the progression system in rim world. Also only the ones with calling can make masterwork(the final tier) equips/food/etc'. So: a calling is a RimWorld-passion-style large XP multiplier, and masterwork (the final tier) output is gated to calling heroes only. Q3 research is parked for the base builder.
2026-09-23 impl (worker): hero.gd adds PROFESSIONS (profession->building id), calling (derived from instance_id hash, no RNG draw), profession_xp (plain seconds), profession_skill / add_profession_xp (x calling_xp_multiplier on earn) / is_profession_master; to_dict adds calling + profession_xp (sorted); from_dict _read_professions derives when missing, warns on unknown calling/profession, errors on bad XP (loads 0). balance rows profession_xp_minutes_per_level=20, profession_skill_cap=5, calling_xp_multiplier=4. Tests: new test_hero_professions.gd (10) + 2 disk round-trips in test_save_service.gd (current + legacy-without-keys then resave). Mutation (loader ignores saved calling) turned both files red. BUILT: gate 0/0; GUT 424/424. Evidence .agent-results/ig-wgj.8/. No commit. Verifier pending (boundary #1).
2026-09-23 director: verifier-hard ACCEPT (pass-with-concerns). Applied F1: add_profession_xp refuses non-finite/negative work_seconds (push_error, no write) + test_bad_work_seconds_are_refused_so_nan_never_reaches_the_save. Accepted as-is: F3 probabilistic re-derive tests (~20% miss, backed by forced-calling disk test), F4 JSON ~14-digit float rounding at thresholds, F5 huge finite XP loads (can't forge a master outside the calling). F2 stale gate log -> director re-runs BUILT before commit.

title: Walk the town as your embodied hero (saved body, protected from spending)
description:
WHY
Owner, 2026-09-23: "we see our heros walking around". GAME_SPEC § The town avatar (ruled 2026-08-13, pinned down 2026-09-23) says the player walks the town as one of their own roster heroes. That hero is swappable, and while embodied it cannot be spent. This bead adds the body and its save state. See ARCHITECTURE.md § The town is the interface and DECISIONS.md 2026-09-23.

BEHAVIOR
1. New hub/town/town_hero.gd: a CharacterBody3D built with heroes/hero_model.gd (from the loader bead).
   - WASD and arrow keys move it, relative to the camera.
   - Clips: Idle when still, Walking_A when moving.
   - A follow camera with zoom.
   - With no body, the town shows the fixed overview camera, as today.
2. Clicking a far building follows the owner's answer to the far-click question. Default: the body walks there, then the panel opens.
   - With no body, a click opens the panel at once.
   - A click never walks the body through a building. Straight line with a stop radius; no navmesh.
3. The hero detail panel gets a "Walk as this hero" button. The HUD gets a "Step out" button.
   - The choice is deliberate. There is no auto-pick.
4. GameSession gets:
   - embodied_hero_id: int, where -1 means none
   - embody_hero(id) -> bool: refused if the hero is busy (is_hero_busy) or not on the roster
   - step_out()
   It emits the existing roster_changed signal. No new signal unless one is needed.
5. Protection:
   - is_hero_protected() (game_session.gd:434) returns true for the body. That makes sacrifice refuse it.
   - Each dispatch entry point refuses a party that contains the body, with a message that names the hero:
     - dispatch_expedition (:526)
     - dispatch_force, via _preview_force_data (:600-622)
     - dispatch_rescue (:833)
     - recover_cache (:166)
   - Grep every is_hero_busy caller first. Any other path that reserves a hero gets the same check.
   - Do NOT fold the body into is_hero_busy(). The body can still be geared, enhanced and ranked up.
6. If the body leaves the roster by any path, the body resets to -1 and the town returns to the overview.

SAVE
- Additive key "embodied_hero_id" in GameSession.to_dict/from_dict (keys around game_session.gd:1824-1844).
- A missing key, a stale id or a busy hero loads as -1.
- Do not bump SAVE_VERSION unless an additive key forces it (P2-23 precedent).

ACCEPTANCE
- It survives save and reload: embody a hero, save through SaveService to disk, reload, and the same hero is the body. Prove it with a real disk round-trip, not to_dict alone.
- A save without the key loads with no body and no error.
- Tests:
  - each dispatch entry point refuses the body
  - sacrifice refuses the body
  - equip, enhance and rank-up on the body are allowed
  - embody_hero refuses a busy hero
  - the body resets when its hero leaves the roster
- BUILT: the import gate shows zero errors and zero warnings, and GUT is green.
- Screenshot evidence of walking and of the follow camera, in .agent-results/<id>/.
- Boundaries #1 (save) and #2 (scene<->script) make a verifier pass mandatory.

title: Arena attack clips are stretched 3-4x to fit the balance windows; trim them instead
description:
Root cause of 'combat feels clunky' after the Mixamo swap (played 2026-09-05, play pass 4).

arena.gd:_play_animation() sets custom_speed = animation.length / target_duration, so every
attack plays the WHOLE Mixamo clip (stance -> windup -> swing -> return to stance) squeezed
into the balance window that was authored for capsules. Measured native lengths (headless,
2026-09-05) against the windows they are forced into:

  Attack_A  1.500 s -> 0.42 s  (3.6x)   light chain
  Attack_B  1.667 s -> 0.42 s  (4.0x)
  Attack_C  1.367 s -> 0.42 s  (3.3x)
  Attack_Heavy 1.000 s -> 0.92 s (1.1x) -- the one that reads fine, and the user agrees
  Standing Dodge Fwd/L/R ~1.0 s -> 0.38 s (2.6x); Backward 1.633 s -> 0.38 s (4.3x)
  Block (enemy parry) 1.400 s -> 0.20 s (7x, a twitch)
  Attack_A (enemy) 1.500 s -> 1.10 s (1.4x) -- but peak extension does not land at the
    0.55 s active onset SYSTEMS.md 'the t ~= 0.55 s alignment target' rules it should
  Hit_Chest (hero) plays at NATIVE 0.767 s but hit stun is 0.35 s, so Idle cuts it in half
  Block (hero) native 1.4 s, parry lasts ~0.65 s, cut mid-raise

The 0.06 s crossfade is a hard cut at 4x. The heavy is the proof: the one clip near native
speed is the one that feels right.

Fix, smallest that works: a per-clip trim table {clip: [start_s, end_s]} in arena.gd.
In _bind_animation_libraries set animation.length = end (Godot Animation has no trim API)
and in _play_animation seek(start) after play(). Stretch the TRIMMED swing segment into the
window, not the whole clip. The Mixamo attacks have ~0.5-0.7 s of actual swing, so light
attacks land near 1.3x instead of 4x. Give hero Hit_Chest a target_duration of
arena_enemy_hit_stun. Trim enemy Block to the shield raise (~0.3 s). Set the enemy Attack_A
trim so its peak lands at t = 0.55 s, which also closes the SYSTEMS.md alignment target.

The trim values need eyes on each clip in the editor (or a played guess, then tune). That
is the authored step; the code is ~20 lines. No AnimationTree, no new clips, no balance
changes. ig-e5u (AnimationTree, 8-way) stays separate and blocked on the backpedal asset.

Acceptance: import gate + GUT green; test_arena.gd's hit-stop resume test still passes
(seek after play must not break assigned_animation resume); a played light chain reads as
three swings, not three twitches; enemy contact reads as caused by the visible blade.
Boundary: none crossed (no save, no scene rename, no autoload). verifier optional.
notes:

Director re-ran both gates on the final tree: import_gate.ps1 exit 0; GUT 204/204 passing.
Files: combat/arena/arena.gd (CLIP_TRIMS table, length trim in bind, seek-on-fresh-start in _play_animation, hero Hit_Chest fitted to arena_enemy_hit_stun), tests/unit/test_arena.gd (span helper, 1 new test).
Stretch now: lights ~1.1-1.7x (was 3.3-4x), dodges ~1.6x (was 2.6-4.3x), enemy Block 1x (was 7x), enemy Attack_A contact at 0.5395 s vs the 0.55 s target.

Finding: Block is a held guard pose with no raise motion at all. A real shield raise needs a new clip; out of scope.

Known ceiling: _play_animation decides 'fresh start' by assigned_animation changing. That is only correct because the state machine always plays Idle/locomotion for at least one frame between two uses of the same clip. If a future state ever chains the same clip back to back, the second play starts from the clip's frame 0 (stance) instead of the trim start. ponytail: fix then by also treating a finished clip as fresh.

title: Timed expeditions, team presets, and bulk management
description:
Objective: replace click-speed expedition farming with concurrent timed dispatches so roster depth and equipped strength improve sustained returns. The user explicitly requested timers, named team presets, send-X-times/auto-repeat, and bulk resource management. This is Astra's proposed direction pending user decisions and a decision-complete Plan-mode specification; it is not an accepted implementation plan.

Each hero may participate in one active expedition. Separate teams run concurrently without an energy meter or arbitrary small dispatch cap. Equipped heroes and their gear are reserved while away, with no mid-run transfers or sacrifice. Show duration before dispatch; derive it from current team strength against mission difficulty with diminishing gains and a nonzero floor. Exact timing and reward tuning are provisional and must cover a fresh save with only three pulls and compare solo with full-team efficiency because current enemies scale with team size.

Preserve combat and permadeath: a past clear is history, not proof of safety. Derive any Safe label from conservative worst-case attrition for the current roster, gear, and zone, including retreat threshold, and validate it before trusting it. Named presets require durable hero identities rather than names or indices, show missing or busy members, and never silently substitute. Preset launch offers one run, a finite total run count, and eventually until-stopped looping. Repeat orders recheck availability and safety, stop on casualty, retreat, or an incomplete team, and support stop-after-current-run. Credit rewards automatically. A dispatch board shows team, zone, remaining time, completed/ordered runs, and cumulative rewards, with collectable reports for review.

Clock behavior awaits the user's async answer. Astra's proposed default is that dispatched missions finish while closed while repeats run only while open; alternatives are session-only timing or bounded repeats progressing offline. Do not assume an answer.

Recovery remains unresolved. The current global expedition-turn clock would let parallel or automatic returns rapidly expire lost gear. Before implementation, explicitly redesign expiry and damage aging while preserving a meaningful Reliquary benefit; do not silently retain or replace the existing rule.

Bulk QoL reuses existing batch salvage/sacrifice and filters. Add protection for favorites, preset members, away heroes, and equipped gear; selection by rank, type, slot, and availability; clear destructive previews with outputs; quantity/all-eligible salvage and sacrifice; and batch part conversion with a keep-at-least reserve. The user's word refine is ambiguous among salvage, part conversion, and enhancement; identify the intended meaning before creating any resource system. No automatic destructive processing by default.

Scope implementation only after design acceptance: (1) timed persisted dispatch, reservations, presets, and finite repeats as one complete player loop; (2) richer bulk management and advanced automation. Existing ig-544 (controlled playable expeditions) and ig-yzc (hop into a sent run) are related direction, but neither grants scope for this work and neither is changed by this epic.

Technical entry points are hub/hub.gd:_on_expedition_pressed/_do_expedition, hub/expedition/expedition.gd:resolve, systems/game_session.gd, systems/save_service.gd, and heroes/hero.gd. Saves are version 1 with no durable hero IDs or migration machinery, and current resolution performs multiple automatic saves. Design exactly-once rewards and casualties, deterministic restart behavior, version-1 migration, and stable completion ordering for concurrent returns. Keep the three-autoload cap, central kill_hero path, and SaveService ownership. Change the explicit no-clock/no-offline-accrual spec only through an accepted plan. In Default mode, do not implement this complex epic until a decision-complete Plan-mode plan is accepted or the user explicitly overrides that gate.

Eventual acceptance: run tests/import_gate.ps1 and the full GUT suite; add focused reservation, repeat, timer, and migration tests plus actual isolated-APPDATA save/reload checks for in-flight missions, duplicate-return prevention, and old saves; visually check populated and empty dispatch boards. Do not mutate the user's save, run concurrent Godot processes, or perform git operations, commits, or pushes. This design/source-inspection turn establishes no runtime proof.
notes:
ACCEPTED DESIGN — 2026-09-21 (user authorized implement-all; direct authorization governs proceeding)

Entry point: core worker starts at systems/game_session.gd + systems/save_service.gd, then deterministic combat/expedition rules and serialization. UI worker separately owns hub/hub.gd, hub/hub.tscn, theme/UI tests and docs; core worker must not edit those paths. Do not close this epic until all core, UI, verification, save/reload, and review gates are complete.

1. Identity/schema: Save version 2. Hero and Item gain stable random serialized instance_id:String and favorite:bool=false. Legacy v1 missing IDs migrate once. Names and indices are never identity. Persist GameSession team_presets:Array[Dictionary], expedition_orders:Array[Dictionary], expedition_reports:Array[Dictionary], recovery_clock_seconds:float, recovery_clock_paused:bool. Presets are {id,name,hero_ids:Array[String],zone_id}; preserve missing/dead references and never substitute. At the v2 trust boundary reject duplicate object IDs, malformed presets/orders, duplicate/invalid teams, unknown/locked dispatch zones, overlapping active teams, invalid finite/count/time/seed state, and do not overwrite canonical save on rejection.

2. Reservations/protection: one hero may be in at most one active order; unlimited disjoint orders. Shared backend guards prevent busy heroes from equip/unequip/rank-up/sacrifice/recovery/arena availability and prevent touching busy equipped gear. kill_hero remains the only roster removal path and must remain usable for expedition deaths; sacrifice guard precedes it. Preset/favorite membership protects heroes from destructive sacrifice; favorite/equipped items protect bulk salvage. Non-destructive equip/enhance remains allowed for non-busy favorites. Revalidate at commit.

3. Timing: combat_ratio=Hero.compute_team_power(team)/(zone.recommended_power*team.size()/5.0). full_team_seconds=max(zone.minimum_duration_seconds,zone.base_duration_seconds/sqrt(combat_ratio)); actual_seconds=ceil(full_team_seconds*5.0/team.size()). Reject empty/invalid/zero-power teams. Author Verdant 60/15, Ashfall 180/45, Sundered 300/75 seconds. Values are provisional pending play; do not alter current reward/combat tuning. Verify equal-gear 1-vs-5 throughput and fresh-three-hero pace.

4. Safety/repeats: forecast emulates worst-case loss damage across Wave.from_zone using exact max HP, rounding, cumulative HP, and non-boss <=25% retreat rule including all traits/stats. Safe only if every hero survives every wave and no retreat. Finite risky dispatch allowed with warning; infinite requires safe and rechecks before every repeat. total_runs is 1..999 including initial; 0 means infinite. Automatically bank every completed run and track cumulative stones/xp/items and runs_completed. Stop after casualty, retreat/failure, incomplete team, or stop_requested; stop means finish current. Captured membership/destination are immutable under preset edits.

5. Clock: persist per-order stable ID, deterministic run seed, initial duration and remaining_seconds. Use monotonic online delta; persist saved_at_unix for offline elapsed max(0, now-saved_at_unix). On load subtract offline time only from already-dispatched current runs; resolve each due run once, then start at most the next repeat at full duration in the open session. No recursive offline catch-up. Rollback gives zero offline progress; forward jump completes current run only. Stable due ordering is remaining time then order ID. Pulse about 0.25s; no per-frame save. Periodic timer/recovery save about 15s and durable dispatch/completion mutations. Pause-menu pause stops online delta; closing follows offline rule. UI observes backend scheduling and need not own it.

6. Exactly once: persisted seed drives deterministic local RNG through expedition/quick-resolve while preserving public resolve(team,wave) seam via helper/optional expedition entry. Defer existing signal-triggered saves during resolution and commit one atomic save containing casualties, cache, rewards, order advance, report. Atomic failure restores pre-transaction memory, preserves previous canonical save, sets notice, and cannot retry awards from mutated memory. Dispatch has the same durability. SaveService remains sole file owner; prevent from_dict/load autosave recursion and preserve newer-version refusal. Add actual isolated-APPDATA reload tests.

7. Recovery: turns remains historical completed/attempted expedition count only. Cache expiry moves to an active recovery clock that runs only in unpaused, active gameplay and never offline. Any new cache pauses recovery_clock_paused. acknowledge_recovery_losses unpauses all current losses. Cache stores its created recovery-clock value. Lifetime seconds=900+300*ReliquaryLevel; damage age converts elapsed active seconds to minutes and reuses 0.03 per unit, Reliquary -0.03/level, and power penalty. Preserve strict <0 expiration. Legacy turn age maps to elapsed active minutes while preserving remaining effective window and migrated caches start paused. Parallel returns/dispatch do not age caches. Recovery acknowledgment is independent from report retention.

8. Reports: retain newest 50. Each summarizes captured team/zone, outcome, casualty names, per-run and cumulative rewards, and stop reason. Rewards never depend on review.

Public backend API: GameSession.hero_by_id(id:String)->Hero; is_hero_busy(hero:Hero)->bool; is_hero_protected(hero:Hero)->bool; is_item_protected(item:Item)->bool; set_hero_favorite(hero:Hero,value:bool)->void; set_item_favorite(item:Item,value:bool)->void; save_team_preset(preset_id:String,preset_name:String,hero_ids:Array[String],zone_id:String)->String; delete_team_preset(id:String)->bool; dispatch_expedition(hero_ids:Array[String],zone_id:String,total_runs:int,team_name:String,preset_id:String='')->String; request_stop_expedition(order_id:String)->void; acknowledge_recovery_losses()->void. ExpeditionOrders.duration_seconds(team:Array[Hero],zone:ZoneDefinition,balance:BalanceTable)->float; safety_forecast(...)->Dictionary {safe:bool,reason:String}. Add `expeditions_changed` for timer/order UI refresh, separate from autosave roster_changed, plus explicit testable tick/offline entry points. Bulk API follows as a separate exact handoff; do not guess it.

Core ownership: heroes/hero.gd, equipment/item.gd, equipment/lost_cache.gd, combat/quick_resolve.gd, hub/expedition/expedition.gd, new hub/expedition/expedition_orders.gd, systems/game_session.gd, systems/save_service.gd, balance_table.gd, balance.tres, zones/zone_definition.gd and three zone definitions as needed, new systems/bulk_operations.gd, backend tests/unit and tests/save_roundtrip_check.gd. ACCEPTED BULK SCOPE — 2026-09-22

Refining means batch operations over the existing salvage, sacrifice, enhancement and part-conversion systems; no new resource system. Public API: GameSession.preview_bulk_salvage(item_ids:Array[String],quantity:int)->Dictionary; preview_bulk_sacrifice(hero_ids:Array[String],target_id:String,quantity:int)->Dictionary; preview_bulk_enhance(item_ids:Array[String],target_level:int,budget_parts:Array[int])->Dictionary; preview_bulk_conversion(rank:int,quantity:int,reserve:int)->Dictionary; commit_bulk_plan(plan:Dictionary)->bool. quantity=0 means all eligible/max convertible; positive is a deterministic exact limit. last_action_error:String is ephemeral.

Plans are read-only dictionaries with shared keys kind, valid, error, entries, excluded, cost_parts[8], gain_parts[8], essence_gain, resonance_gain, parameters. Entries carry stable IDs, names, rank and operation-specific before/after/spend/gain fields; excluded entries carry id/name/reason. Commit rebuilds from the current profile and refuses any stale eligibility, protection, membership, cost/output, Forge, target, gear, rank or resource change. One SaveService-backed memory/disk transaction commits the whole batch or rolls it all back on write failure. No generic action/plugin framework.

All pure selection/arithmetic lives in new static res://hub/bulk_operations.gd; GameSession supplies profile state and applies coordinated mutations. Reuse the existing single-item formulas. Salvage/sacrifice exclude favorites, preset members, busy heroes, equipped gear/fodder; sacrifice excludes recipient. Selected/displayed order is deterministic and quantity never fills from unselected resources. Preview exact parts/essence/resonance.

Enhancement permits favorite inventory items, bounds target by current Forge cap, accepts eight nonnegative per-rank budgets also capped by actual parts, and processes each selected item to target before the next. Skip target <= current with reason. No random/new enhancement mechanic. Conversion accepts source ranks 0..6, preserves reserve, computes max=floor(max(0,parts[rank]-reserve)/3), refuses positive quantity above max, spends 3 per output, and never cascades. Add focused backend tests for protection, stale plans, funds, budget/reserve and atomic failure.

design:
ASTRA IMPLEMENTATION PLAN — AUTONOMOUS SQUAD COMBAT AND RESCUE
2026-09-22. Product direction approved by owner: implement every suggestion in the squad-command design and downed/rescue follow-up; use Sol and Luna in parallel. This is the decision-complete implementation proposal. Implementation authorized and active: the owner explicitly removed the global mode blocker. This design is the accepted contract; runtime acceptance remains outstanding.

OBJECTIVE
Replace the future direct-control expedition direction with autonomous, watchable, commandable hero combat integrated with existing timed orders. Deliver standard five-hero expeditions, a 30-hero raid and a 50-hero regional mission, four archetype ability kits, configurable automation and supplies, downed revival, stranded-hero rescue/abandonment, and safe persistent watched/background/offline settlement. The existing action arena remains an isolated legacy practice scene until the new scene passes acceptance; the hub then presents RTS practice/watch as the primary combat surface.

DIRECTOR PRODUCT RULINGS
1. Heroes always handle basic attacks and role positioning. Auto Battle advances mission objectives; players may override orders at any time. Per-ability and per-item Auto/Manual preferences remain effective in either mode. Squad stances: advance, stay together, defend, protect ally. Direct orders take priority until fulfilled/cancelled. Tactical pause affects the watched battle only; leaving the view resumes it. No live speed multiplier in this implementation.
2. RTS controls: LMB selection/drag box, Shift additive selection, RMB contextual move/attack/guard/carry, Shift+A attack-move, H hold, G guard targeting, R retreat, Space battle pause, 1-9 squad selection and double-tap camera focus; WASD pan and wheel zoom. Selected hero/squad actions appear in one compact command panel. The battlefield uses orthographic perspective, authored ground/bounds, native chibi primitive meshes, class silhouettes, faction/selection rings, HP/downed markers, restrained skill effects and clear danger markers.
3. Existing archetypes receive one signature active and one passive, authored in Resources: Knight protection, Ranger piercing shot, Mage area burst, Rogue flank/interrupt. Automatic decisions use these exact kit rules. Ability data includes cooldown, range, effect/radius and magnitude; no new hero stat. The first consumables are healing and revival draughts; configured per-run allocations, auto-use conditions, last-revival reserve, and stockpile keep-at-least reserves. Consumables are escrowed at dispatch; unused allocations return once at settlement. Repeat refill must respect reserves and stop with a visible reason when it cannot satisfy the configured loadout.
4. Zero HP means downed, never immediate roster deletion in this backend. Living allies revive via the configured skill/item rules; any living ally in the full deployed force keeps the battle active. Victory secures all surviving/downed allies. Retreat extracts living heroes and downed heroes actually carried to the exit; unrecovered heroes become stranded. Downed heroes do not attack, move or consume supplies.
5. A full wipe or abandoned battlefield survivors creates a stranded incident. Hero IDs remain in the roster but are unavailable and protected, with equipment reserved. Player chooses rescue or explicit abandonment; no automatic rescue dispatch. A rescue team of up to five enters the preserved battlefield, reaches fallen heroes and extracts them. It can use revival or carry a downed hero to the exit. It need not kill every enemy. Extracted heroes are secured; withdrawn rescuers return; wiped rescuers join the stranded incident. Existing gear-cache recovery is a separate feature. Only final abandonment/expiry invokes the established Expedition -> GameSession.kill_hero removal/cache path.
6. Stranded incidents use active-play rescue time, separate from gear-cache state. New incident pauses its countdown for review; explicit Start rescue window starts it. Lifetime uses the existing authored 900 + 300*Reliquary seconds as a provisional starting value, not offline elapsed time. Failed attempts do not reset incident age. A deadline prevents dispatching new attempts once expired; an already-dispatched rescue is allowed to resolve. Original and later stranded heroes share the incident deadline. Closing the game never consumes this window. No passive rescue while unreviewed.
7. Reuse 1-5 member presets as squads. Standard zones permit one squad; the new Fallen Citadel raid permits up to six squads/30 heroes; Frontier March regional mission permits up to ten squads/50 heroes. CLOCKS / MIGRATION / PAUSE
Route minimum and battle advance in parallel from dispatch. Active order phases are fighting, rescuing, or returning; a terminal battle enters returning until remaining_seconds reaches zero, then one settlement removes/repeats the order. A wiped battle can settle its stranded incident as soon as its terminal state is committed; it does not wait for an artificial trip home. UI calls remaining_seconds the route minimum while fighting, not a promised exact arrival. A repeat starts both a fresh full route and a fresh battle; excess delta is never spent on the next run. Standard encounter maximum is 180 logical seconds, raid 300, region 420; timeout ends as withdrawal, returns living actors, and strands downed actors not extracted. Offline route advances by all nonnegative elapsed time; combat advances by at most its remaining authored simulation bound, current run only. Recovery/rescue clocks never receive offline time.
For v2 migration: validate v2 using its original rules, transform stable fields, reduce its remaining route by max(now-old_saved_at,0) once, create new battle at logical tick zero, then atomically persist v3 with the new timestamp. No historical combat ticks are invented, even if the route is already zero. Do not then apply ordinary v3 offline advancement again. v0/v1 follow existing identity migration before this transform. Migration failure blocks play/writes and leaves canonical bytes intact.
Tactical pause is a nonserialized GameSession set of watched order IDs. It pauses combat ticks only, not the route minimum or other orders. Leaving the battle view, changing watched order, loading a profile, or restarting clears it. The paused-view reload test must assert resumed simulation with preserved durable combat state; it must not expect the pause flag to persist.

title: Base builder and NPC-driven economy (direction only, needs owner rulings)
description:
WHY
Owner, 2026-09-23: "i eventually want it to be a base builder as well, with its own npc driven economy + other features." This epic holds that direction. It is not ready to split, because three rulings decide its shape and each one changes the save format.

It stands alone, not under ig-wgj, so it does not hold the town epic open. It is blocked by the walk, ambient and building visual beads, so it stays out of bd ready until the town exists to build on.

OWNER RULINGS NEEDED (see GAME_SPEC.md § The town hub, base builder direction)
1. Placement. Choices: free placement on a grid; fixed plots you unlock; or keep the fixed layout and only upgrade. Free placement makes building positions save state.
2. What the economy makes. Choices: NPC workers produce goods that feed existing systems (supplies, materials); or a new currency; or only boosts to existing building effects.
3. Offline progress. GAME_SPEC § Hard constraints rules out offline timers and idle income. Default: the economy runs only while you play. Changing that is a spec change, not a ticket.

ARCHITECTURE NOTES (ARCHITECTURE.md § The town is the interface)
- No fourth autoload. Economy state lives on GameSession and saves through SaveService like everything else.
- Economy rules are pure functions under hub/ (or a new systems file), tested without a scene.
- Townsfolk that do work need an owner ruling on § Scope boundaries first.
- Also parks "defend the town" so it has a home.

ACCEPTANCE (for this epic)
- The three rulings are recorded in GAME_SPEC.md.
- tech-lead splits the epic into beads, each with why, files, behavior, acceptance including survives save and reload, and non-goals.
- No code is written under this epic before the split.

NON-GOALS
any code; any save change before the rulings.
notes: 2026-09-23: the owner ruled that heroes are the shopkeepers (GAME_SPEC § Heroes staff the buildings). Keeper professions are the labor this economy would read: more slots per building means more keepers, and production scales with keeper skill. Non-roster workers still need a Scope-boundaries ruling.
